title: Exploring GPU-to-GPU Communication: Insights into Supercomputer Interconnects
problem: Multi-GPU nodes in exascale supercomputers use diverse interconnect technologies with varying bandwidths and design choices, making it challenging to assess performance expectations and identify optimization opportunities across different systems.
motivation: Optimizing GPU-to-GPU communication is essential for achieving efficiency and maximizing resource utilization in multi-GPU exascale supercomputing systems.
method: The paper characterizes three exascale supercomputers (Alps, Leonardo, LUMI) with distinct architectures using a comprehensive benchmark suite targeting both intra-node and inter-node GPU communication. Performance evaluation scales to 4,096 GPUs, analyzing interconnect limitations and identifying optimization opportunities at network and software layers.
key_novelty: Comprehensive comparative characterization of GPU-to-GPU communication performance across multiple exascale supercomputers with diverse interconnect technologies and architectural designs.
contributions: Characterization of GPU interconnects on three distinct exascale supercomputers (Alps, Leonardo, LUMI)
Performance evaluation of intra-node and inter-node communication scaling to 4,096 GPUs
Identification of untapped bandwidth and optimization opportunities ranging from network to software layers
Practical guidance for researchers, system architects, and software developers on multi-GPU supercomputing

metrics.other: bandwidth utilization, communication latency and throughput

limitations: Limitations and scope constraints are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: GPU interconnect performance characterization for exascale systems
